# components/accounting/packs/

## Purpose
Renders a `PackDocument` (from `services/packs/packDocument.ts`) as React — both the interactive preview and the `?print=1` page the PDF pipeline photographs. No figures are computed here; the component tree only lays out what the document model already holds.

## Caller contract
`pages/accounting/reports/report-packs.tsx` is a dispatcher: `isPrintRender(router)` decides between the interactive screen and `PackPrintPage`. The interactive screen renders `SectionCard` from here; the print path renders a `PackDocument` through `PackSectionView`. **The two share their FORMATTERS, not their markup** — `packMappers`, `formatPackKv` and `scorecardFigure` — which is what keeps a figure reading the same on both without pinning them to one layout. The print page renders WITHOUT `AppLayout` and fetches exactly the two paths `packPrintApiPaths` authorises.

## Main signatures
- `PackPrintPage({ packType, from, to })` — the whole of `?print=1`
- `SectionCard({ section, defaultOpen })` (`PackSectionCard.tsx`) — the INTERACTIVE preview of one section, not the printed one
- `PackPrintView({ document })` · `PackSectionView` · `PackCover` · `PackToc` · `PackChart`
- `usePackPrintData(packType, from, to)` — the print page's two fetches
- `usePrintMode(enabled)` · `usePrintReady(dataReady, expectedCharts)` · `countCharts(sections)` · `countPageModelCharts(pages)`
- `PackPagesView({ document })` — the twelve-page `PackPagesDocument` renderer (`pages/`, `primitives/`); `PackBlocks({ page, scale })` · `PackBlockView({ block, scale })`
- `formatPackKv(item): string`

## Business rules
- **The PAGE owns print mode, not the renderer.** `usePrintMode` adds `print-mode` to `<html>` and removes `.dark` in a LAYOUT effect: `ThemeContext` defaults to dark and sets the class in a passive mount effect, so a child that merely removes it is overwritten a frame later and the PDF prints white on white. The Gotenberg transport cannot run a script on our behalf, which is why this cannot live in the renderer.
- **The scale is REQUIRED at every level of the page tree.** `PackPagesView` narrows `document.numberConvention.scale` with `toMoneyScale` and THROWS on an unrecognised value rather than falling back — printing unscaled cells under a header that says `R'000` is a 1000x misread on a document a director forwards to a bank. Every primitive's `scale` prop and `formatFigureText`'s scale argument are non-optional, so a renderer that forgets fails `tsc`.
- **Commentary is labelled by source, in text.** `NarrativeColumns` renders a body for `approved` (a human signed it) and `derived` (deterministic code) only, each under its own visible source line — R7 admits derived text because it is deterministic, not because anyone signed it, so a reader must be able to tell them apart without relying on colour. `draft` renders NOTHING: no node, not hidden by CSS. `pending` renders a placeholder.
- **`PackBlockView`'s switch is exhaustive, enforced by a `never` assignment.** There is deliberately no runtime "unknown kind" branch: a `PackPageBlock` is only ever constructed in the same process that renders it (R-P41) and never parsed from JSON, so an unknown kind cannot reach the renderer without first failing `tsc`.
- **The twelve pages are not twelve components.** Spec §4.A's pages differ in WHICH blocks they carry, not in how a block is drawn; the management pack (WS4c) reuses pages 1-8 wholesale. Only the cover and the contents have their own layout components, dispatched by page number in `PackPagesView`; their model blocks still render inside them.
- **The readiness gate has no timeout on purpose.** `[data-print-ready="true"]` is set only when the data has loaded AND every chart has drawn an `<svg>`. A pack missing a chart is a document sent to a client with a hole in it; a hard render timeout is the loud, diagnosable failure we want instead.
- A margin with no meaning renders through `marginKvItem`/`formatPackKv`, never as `0.0%`.
- **`apiFetch` RESOLVES on a 4xx** (see `src/lib/apiFetch.ts`), so a status check is not optional on this screen. A 429 used to fall through to `.json()`, yield an envelope with no `data`, and leave the page blank — indistinguishable from a company with no ledger. The pack request checks the status first and shows a `role="status"` notice, naming the wait when `Retry-After` is present (it is not today; `apiResponse.tooManyRequests` sets no such header).
- **Only the NEWEST pack request may paint.** Switching pack type or nudging a date leaves two in flight, and a wide-period aggregation outlives a narrow one — so the last answer used to win, showing one pack's figures under another's heading with the download buttons pointed elsewhere. Each effect run marks itself stale on cleanup.
- **`router.query.pack` is VALIDATED, not cast — and ABSENT is not WRONG.** No `pack` at all means the management pack, which is what `?print=1` has always meant and what old bookmarks rely on. A pack that is PRESENT but not a known type is refused: `isPackType` (`services/packs/packSections.ts`) checks it against the same map the pack labels come from, and an empty `?pack=` or a repeated one (which arrives as an array) counts as present and wrong. It used to be `String(...) as PackType`, which typed a lie and sent whatever the URL said on to build a trend URL. Like the data-error state, the refusal never becomes print-ready — the renderer times out loudly rather than photographing the wrong document.
- `_app.tsx` gates `AuthProvider`, `CompanyProvider` and the analytics tracker off a print render — see `src/lib/pdf/.claude.md` for what each of those fetches costs mid-render. The gate is scoped to this page's path, so another page's `?print=1` is unaffected.
- **`getServerSideProps` on the pack page is what makes the dispatch safe.** Without it Next statically optimises the page: the server renders with an empty `router.query` and picks the interactive screen while the client's first pass reads `?print=1` and picks `PackPrintPage`, so hydration fails — and `router.query` stays `{}` until `router.isReady`, which is long enough for a provider's mount effect to fire and clear the print token's cookie. With it, `router.isReady` is true from the first client render, so `isPrintRender` reads `router.query` and nothing else; there is no not-ready window to paper over.
